thread:
Jamal: Heads up - after yesterday's runtime rollout (matmul-tiling-v2 + attn-vec-opt-level=3 + quant-profile=hybrid-int4) we're seeing a ~22% drop in prefix-cache hit rate for several customer workloads. Latency warmup spike on first 10 tokens. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/PRFX/cache-hit-heatmap

Maria: ugh. which models/variants? any pattern by seq len or batch?

Jamal: mostly ff1/ff1-large (bfloat fallback path), heavy short-priming prompts (<=64). hit rate pre-rollout ~86% -> post ~64%. median p50 latency for first-token went 28ms -> 95ms.

Alex: can you dump a few raw cache keys (hashed) and the tokenizer-normalized inputs? suspect normalization changed with the tokenizer-lite tweak.

Jamal: pasted sample logs below (redacted):
```\n[2026-03-17T22:12:03Z] req=ae3f pid=42 model=ff1-large variant=matmul-tiling-v2 quant=hybrid-int4 seq=48 priming=system+user
cache_lookup: key_hash=0x8f3a1b tokenized_prefix=\"\\u0120Hello , world\" normalized=\" Hello, world\" hit=false
kv_store_probe: shard=3 bucket=0x1c2 mismatch_reason=prefix_mismatch
```\n```\n[2026-03-17T22:12:04Z] req=be12 pid=47 model=ff1-large variant=matmul-tiling-v2 quant=hybrid-int4 seq=12 priming=system
cache_lookup: key_hash=0x9f1b2c tokenized_prefix=\"\\u0120Hello , world\" normalized=\" Hello , world\" hit=true
```

Maria: hmm keys look similar but normalized forms differ (comma spacing). Are we using different tokenizer config when computing the canonical key vs when generating the warmup key?

Priya: perf note: matmul-tiling-v2 changes request packing alignment; batching boundary shift might reorder tokens when generating the cheap warmup cache entries vs the real request path. That could change key canonicalization if we rely on byte offsets.

Sara: pulled profiler traces. attaching short summary: heatmap shows warmup writes concentrated on gpu0:prefetch-thread but lookups go to gpu2 at first token. Our smart-router is sending priming requests to cheaper capacity pool (fallback) while later tokens hit main pool. If key generation includes an internal pool-id or build-id, that explains misses.

Bobby: could this be a build-id embedded in the key? last week's compile changed kernel-abi minor version and we did a hot-restart; some components still have old build-id in metadata.

Jamal: I grepped: key schema v3 = join([model, variant, quant, tokenizer_hash, normalized_prefix]) -> hashed. tokenizer_hash uses tokenizer config checksum at cold start. Looks like compiler heuristics changed tokenizer-lite checksum path (we accidentally include `matmul-tiling-v2` flag in tokenizer checksum calculation).

Maria: that's a clear bug - kernel flags leaking into tokenizer_checksum. Can we patch quickly to ignore runtime flags? what's the blast radius?

Alex: patch idea: decouple tokenizer_checksum -> solely tokenizer assets + normalization rules. Add compatibility translation layer that maps old keys to canonicalized normalized_prefix (expensive but safe). We'll need to backfill popular prefixes for 48h window.

Priya: operational workaround: route priming/warmup traffic to same pool as main inference for the next 24h (force-affinity) to avoid cross-pool mismatches. We can add a temporary header on frontend: `X-Force-Pool: pool-<model>-ff1`.

Jamal: I've run a quick sim on subset: forcing affinity recovers hit rate to 84% for sample traces. Posting small script we used to replay:
```\n# replay warmup trace forcing pool affinity
for req in sample_reqs.json; do 
  curl -XPOST https://api.redwood.local/infer -H \"X-Force-Pool: pool-ff1\" -d \"$req\"
done
```

Maria: action list: 1) rollback tokenizer-checksum change in runtime build (PR#7643) - Maria 2) short-term router affinity - Priya 3) backfill translation lookup for keys - Alex 4) add unit test asserting tokenizer_checksum unaffected by kernel flags - Jamal

Alex: note on backfill: we'll need to store translation mapping like {old_hash -> canonical_norm_prefix_hash} in a small LRU store and warm the primary KV with canonical entries. That needs ~2-4 hours of offline ingestion for top N prefixes per customer.

Bobby: QA: any risk of double-writes causing eviction thrash during backfill? our eviction policy is size-based; short window but might spike writes. coordinate with infra.

Priya: infra: I'll bump kv-store write rate cap and monitor eviction metrics. Also enabling debug logging for cache_key_gen for 6h.

deploy-bot: matmul-tiling-v2 rollout detected at 2026-03-17T21:50Z. Canary passed.

Maria: plan: revert tokenizer-checksum change in next patch set and ship compatibility mapper in same deployment to avoid prolonged misses. Can we schedule the revert in 30m?

Priya: let's do staged revert: canary on 1 node, run replay against canary for 15m, if hit-rate improves push to rest. I'll coordinate deploy windows and monitor grafana panel.

Jamal: putting links: replay script gist: https://git.internal/redwood/replay/warmup-fix, panel: https://grafana.redwood/d/PRFX/cache-hit-heatmap?orgId=1&from=now-6h

Sara: quick follow-up: let's add a short-term metric for \"prefetch_pool_affinity_mismatch\" with a tag for pool_id so we can attr misses to cross-pool warmups.

Bobby: adding to monitoring backlog.

Maria: thanks all. I'll open PR for revert + unit tests. Assigning PR reviewers: Alex, Jamal.

Jamal: ping me when canary metrics look good and I'll trigger the backfill for top prefixes.

Alex: noted - I'll prototype translation mapper this afternoon.

Priya: rolling canary in 12m. Will post updates here. :thumbsup:

Jamal: update: canary reverted + affinity forced on canary node. After 10m: hit rate on canary up to 85% (from 63%). Pushing revert cluster-wide now.

Priya: cluster-wide revert complete. Monitoring.

Bobby: observed temporary write spike during backfill window but eviction remained <2%. all green so far.

Maria: closing loop: will follow up with postmortem and checklist to ensure kernel flags don't leak into unrelated checksums.

Jamal: thanks everyone.
